title: EEG-Based Biometric Authentication
subtitle: Low-channel wearable EEG · Research prototype
summary: A biometric authentication prototype exploring stimulus-evoked EEG responses and Riemannian representations.

details.overview: The work explores EEG-based biometric authentication using a low-channel wearable headset and personalized visual stimuli. The research examined stimulus-evoked responses, including P300, and Riemannian representations for verification.
contributions: Research and development of an EEG authentication prototype
Exploration of stimulus-evoked responses and Riemannian representations
Work with the Emotiv Insight 2 acquisition ecosystem
details.results: A working prototype is described in the source notes. Quantitative evaluation and production-readiness claims are intentionally not asserted here.
challenges: Validation with a limited number of channels
lessons: Biometric research requires careful experimental design
Signal quality and evaluation methodology are central to trustworthy results
researchTitles: EEG-Based Biometric Authentication Using Low-Channel Wearable EEG: A Feasibility Study of Stimulus-Evoked Responses and Riemannian Representations
